saws_warning_scheme.description: SAWS Impact-Based Severe Weather Warning System (IBSWWS): warnings are about 'what the weather will do' rather than 'what the weather will be'. The colour ('robot' traffic-light coding) and number come from combining the level of impact with the likelihood of that impact happening. The forecaster judges the possible impact of a hazard with input from local disaster managers, then uses NWP models and local knowledge of antecedent conditions to judge likelihood. SAWS says the levels only show where the warning sits in the impact-likelihood matrix and are unrelated to tornado ratings. It was developed with the NDMC and piloted with disaster managers before going public. The previous system used purely meteorological thresholds (e.g. strong-wind warning at 35 kt / ~70 km/h).
saws_warning_scheme.introduced: Not confirmed from an official source here. The SAWS FAQ describes a pilot phase with disaster managers but gives no launch date. The ~2019 date is unverified (web search budget ran out before this could be checked).
saws_warning_scheme.levels_source_note: The level-to-colour mapping comes from the SAWS website's own map-styling code (https://www.weathersa.co.za/assets/index-4PCKC_eZ.js): 'warning level 1/2/3/4/7' = yellow rgba(255,255,0); 'warning level 5/6/8/9' = orange rgba(255,165,0); 'warning level 10' = red rgba(255,0,0); 'warning advisory' = purple. The impact axis labels (e.g. minimal/minor/significant/severe) were not found in an official source.

access_notes: EM-DAT: event-level data (DisNo) needs a login at public.emdat.be. Only the public HDX annual country-profile aggregates were used (emdat_country_profile_aggregates), so there are no per-event EM-DAT rows. ReliefWeb: website and disaster pages return HTTP 403 to automated fetch, and the API needs an approved appname (403). ReliefWeb items come from search-result snippets plus the GLIDE registry (glidenumber.net was fully accessible: 13 ZAF records since 2016, of which the flood/storm-relevant ones are included). DFO: the old Archives pages (MasterListrev.htm, index.html) return 410 Gone and arbitrary Cargo API queries are denied. The SA country page on the new DFO wiki was readable (76 events total; 23 since 2016); the DFO archive ends around Feb/Mar 2024. The HDX DFO mirror is stale (2019). GDACS: API fully accessible (61 SA flood events 2016-2026, GLOFAS-driven; many are small Green alerts). FloodList: SA tag index readable (tag pages 2-4 via WebFetch; direct scripted requests got a 202 bot challenge). The last SA article is 26 Sep 2023 and the last article on the whole site is ~3 Jun 2024, so there is no FloodList coverage of Dec 2023 onwards. Non-event FloodList articles (opinion/science pieces, Mozambique-only Dineo items) were left out. NDMC/COGTA: cogta.gov.za has a bad TLS certificate chain (fetched with curl -k); both May 2026 classification pages now return 404. Gazette notice numbers were not retrieved for any event. Stats SA: statssa.gov.za blocked by Incapsula, so Census 2022 language by province was NOT obtained (Census 2011 fallback supplied from the official dashboard API). SAWS: the site is a JS single-page app; the FAQ text and warning-level colour map were taken from its JS bundle, and no official introduction date was found. The web search quota (200/session) ran out partway through, which limited verification of the May 2026 classification, the SAWS launch date and SA flood-fatality database papers. No dedicated SA flood-fatality database paper was found via Crossref.
